name: Question 5
problem:
Find the acute angle between the vector $x$ and the subspace spanned by the linearly independent vectors ${{a}_{1},{a}_{2}},$ where

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,\,x=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -5 \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Round the answer to $2$ decimal places.
worked_solution:
The orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace spanned by the columns of a matrix $A$ is given by

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x=A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T}\,x.
$$

In our case, we have

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ {a}_{1} & {a}_{2} \\ | & |\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 2 & 1 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}]\,⟹\,{A}^{T}=[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

 

Therefore, we get the following projection: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 2 & 1 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}]\cdot {([\begin{aligned}2 & 2 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 2 & 1 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}])}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 & 2 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}5 \\ -5 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 2 & 1 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}]\cdot {[\begin{aligned}8 & 0 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}]}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 \\ -12\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 2 & 1 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{8} & 0 \\ 0 & \frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 \\ -12\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 2 & 1 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 \\ -4\end{aligned}] \\  & =4[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

 

The acute angle between $x$ and $S$ is the acute angle between $x$ and ${\text{proj}}_{S}x.$ Equivalently, it is the acute angle between $x$ and any non-zero vector that is parallel to ${\text{proj}}_{S}x.$ So, to make calculations easier, we can find the angle between the vectors

$\,$ $x=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -5 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,\frac{1}{4}\,{\text{proj}}_{S}x=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

Computing the cosine using the dot product, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{x\cdot {\text{proj}}_{S}x}{‖x‖‖{\text{proj}}_{S}x‖} \\  & =\frac{5\cdot 1+(-5)\cdot (-1)+2\cdot 1}{\sqrt{{5}^{2}+(-5)^{2}+{2}^{2}}\cdot \sqrt{{1}^{2}+(-1)^{2}+{1}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{12}{\sqrt{54}\sqrt{3}} \\  & =\frac{12}{9\sqrt{2}} \\  & =\frac{4}{3\sqrt{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, 

$$
\theta =\operatorname{arccos}⁡(\frac{4}{3\sqrt{2}})≈{19.47}^{∘},
$$

which is already an acute angle.

Question 5
?

Find the acute angle between the vector x and the subspace spanned by the linearly independent vectors {a1,a2}, where a1=[220],a2=[−11−1],x=[5−52].

Round the answer to 2 decimal places.

a
18.88∘
b
17.36∘
c
20.02∘
d
19.47∘
e
21.83∘
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The orthogonal projection of x onto the subspace spanned by the columns of a matrix A is given by projSx=A(ATA)−1ATx.

In our case, we have A=[||a1a2||]=[2−1210−1]⟹AT=[220−11−1].

Therefore, we get the following projection:

projSx=[2−1210−1]⋅([220−11−1]⋅[2−1210−1])−1⋅[220−11−1]⋅[5−52]=[2−1210−1]⋅[8003]−1⋅[0−12]=[2−1210−1]⋅[180013]⋅[0−12]=[2−1210−1]⋅[0−4]=4[1−11].

The acute angle between x and S is the acute angle between x and projSx. Equivalently, it is the acute angle between x and any non-zero vector that is parallel to projSx. So, to make calculations easier, we can find the angle between the vectors

x=[5−52] and 14projSx=[1−11].

Computing the cosine using the dot product, we obtain

cos⁡θ=x⋅projSx‖x‖‖projSx‖=5⋅1+(−5)⋅(−1)+2⋅152+(−5)2+22⋅12+(−1)2+12=12543=1292=432

Therefore,

θ=arccos⁡(432)≈19.47∘,

which is already an acute angle.
